identity.title: POCUS cardiac: qualitative LV systolic function (normal / reduced / severely reduced; EPSS as adjunct) in PLAX/A4C

technique.how: Phased-array probe; parasternal long axis, short axis and apical 4-chamber. Judge endocardial excursion and wall thickening and grade LV function as normal, reduced or severely reduced by eye. Adjunct: in PLAX M-mode through the mitral tip, measure E-point septal separation; >7 mm suggests reduced EF.
technique.prerequisites: Trained operator; at least two adequate views; interpret in the context of heart rate, preload and regional wall-motion.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay resuscitation for imaging in an unstable patient.

interpretation.positive_finding: A visually reduced or severely reduced LV in the hands of a trained emergency clinician agrees with expert assessment (pooled sensitivity 89%, LR+ 6) and shifts a hypotensive or dyspneic patient toward cardiogenic shock/ADHF; EPSS >7 mm is 100% sensitive for EF <=30% in one ED cohort.
interpretation.negative_finding: A visually normal LV makes severe systolic dysfunction unlikely (pooled LR- 0.13) but does not exclude diastolic HF, valvular disease, or a regional infarct; EPSS <=7 mm argues against severe systolic dysfunction (spec 52%).
interpretation.pitfalls: Sepsis, tachycardia and preload change alter apparent function; mitral stenosis, aortic regurgitation and LVH invalidate EPSS. Agreement is moderate for the intermediate 'reduced' category and poorer with limited training or poor windows (22% poor quality in Moore 2002).
interpretation.changes_what: Severely reduced LV with hypotension: treat as cardiogenic shock (inotrope, cardiology, limit fluids); a normal hyperdynamic LV points to hypovolemic/distributive causes and permits fluids.

estimates.target_condition: Abnormal (reduced) LV systolic function, normal vs abnormal, by visual estimation
estimates.population: ED patients; 7 studies, 786 scans; ED clinician sonographers vs expert sonographer
estimates.reference_standard: Expert sonographer (cardiologist/comprehensive echo) assessment of LVSF
estimates.quote: sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio of 89% (95% CI, 80-94%), 85% (95% CI, 80-89%), 5.98 (95% CI, 4.13-8.68) and 0.13 (95% CI, 0.06-0.24)

estimates.target_condition: Severe LV systolic dysfunction (LVEF <=30%) by EPSS >7 mm
estimates.population: Convenience sample of ED patients receiving comprehensive TTE; scans by 3 ED ultrasound fellows
estimates.reference_standard: Calculated LVEF from comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 1.00/(1-0.516); LR- = (1-1.00)/0.516 from sens/spec in abstract
estimates.quote: EPSS measurement of greater than 7 mm for severe systolic dysfunction (LVEF<=30%) were 100.0% (95% confidence interval, 62.9-100.0) and 51.6% (95% confidence interval, 38.6-64.5)

sources.citation: Albaroudi B, Haddad M, Albaroudi O, Abdel-Rahman ME, Jarman R, Harris T. Assessing left ventricular systolic function by emergency physician using point of care echocardiography compared to expert: systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Emerg Med. 2022;29(1):18-32.

McKaigney CJ, Krantz MJ, La Rocque CL, Hurst ND, Buchanan MS, Kendall JL. E-point septal separation: a bedside tool for emergency physician assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction. Am J Emerg Med. 2014;32(6):493-497.

Moore CL, Rose GA, Tayal VS, Sullivan DM, Arrowood JA, Kline JA. Determination of left ventricular function by emergency physician echocardiography of hypotensive patients. Acad Emerg Med. 2002;9(3):186-193.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use eyeball EF to exclude ACS, valvular emergency or tamponade; do not apply EPSS with mitral stenosis, aortic regurgitation, or marked septal hypertrophy.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Severely reduced LV function with hypotension or pulmonary edema: treat as cardiogenic shock, obtain ECG/troponin immediately, and involve cardiology; consider mechanical support pathways.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Pooled kappa 0.68 (normal/abnormal) and weighted kappa 0.70 (three categories) vs experts (Albaroudi 2021); Moore 2002: EP-cardiologist weighted kappa 0.61, cardiologist-cardiologist r 0.84, with 22% of studies rated poor quality.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency clinicians with focused echo training (as in included studies, often ultrasound fellows or credentialed EPs); the intermediate 'reduced' grade is least reliable and hypotensive patients yield more poor-quality windows.

extraction_notes: Primary pooled estimate from Albaroudi 2021 abstract (visual-estimation subgroup, 7 studies; reference standard is expert sonographer agreement, not an outcome). EPSS estimate from McKaigney 2014 abstract; LRs computed (spec CI wide, n small). Moore 2002 (anchor) reports only correlation (r=0.86) and weighted kappa 0.61 in hypotensive patients, so no sens/spec estimate is attached; it is cited for the hypotensive-population reliability statement. Albaroudi full text is PMC OA but per-study tables were not needed for the pooled values.
